audit_findings.title: Finance-lease reinvestment may bypass the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025: $50 million principal repayments, $74 million ROU additions and $36 million amortization; principal repayments equal 26.2% of anchor OE. H1 2026 ROU additions were $178 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease amortization enters the D&A addback, while noncash ROU additions bypass reported capital expenditures and principal repayments remain financing cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we received $577 million in proceeds from the issuance of long-term debt, used $200 million to repurchase shares of our common stock under the stock repurchase plan, used $180 million to repay debt, used $50 million to repay finance lease obligations, used $25 million to repay revolving credit facilities, used $9 million to pay employee taxes on net settlement of equity awards, and used $2 million to pay debt issuance costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate potentially material lease reinvestment outside cash capital expenditures. The record does not establish whether the OE workpaper separately deducted additions or principal. If neither was deducted, OE is overstated; using FY2025 principal as a recurring sensitivity would reduce base operating value by approximately $703 million, or $5.96 per share.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile finance-lease ROU additions, amortization, interest and principal for every historical year; deduct either sustainable asset additions or principal, excluding interest and avoiding double counting, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized contract-fulfillment spending may be omitted from reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash contract-acquisition and fulfillment additions may bypass property capital expenditures, while their amortization is already included in operating expense; any omitted net investment overstates OE and potentially the growth return economics.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalizes direct and incremental costs incurred to obtain and to fulfill a contract in advance of revenue recognition, such as certain labor, third-party service and related product costs.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization is demonstrated, but omission from OE is not. Contract assets increased by a computed $38 million in FY2025, from $233 million to $271 million, and by another $18 million in H1 2026. The $38 million balance increase equals 19.9% of anchor OE, showing material capability, but it is not an adjustment amount because additions, amortization, impairment and currency effects are not separately provided.
audit_findings.action: Obtain annual contract-cost additions, cash payments, amortization, impairments, disposals and currency effects for 2021-2026; identify amounts absent from OE and rerun with sustainable net contract investment.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated capital economics and cash
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 NCI income was $4 million and June 2026 NCI equity was $35 million, equal to 2.1% of anchor OE and 1.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings are combined with consolidated D&A, capex and cash; consolidated addbacks and cash can overstate parent value, while consolidated reinvestment deductions can understate it.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of GXO Logistics, Inc. and its majority-owned subsidiaries and variable interest entities where the Company is the primary beneficiary.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is real, but the filed NCI scale is too small to change the valuation conclusion: the $35 million balance-sheet claim is about $0.30 per diluted share versus base value of $29.24 and market price of $48.32.
audit_findings.action: Document the parent-attributable shares of D&A, capex, contract investment and cash, or deduct the full NCI economic claim; rerun only if that reconciliation reveals exposure materially above the filed NCI scale.

audit_findings.title: A final Italian settlement contaminates the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $65 million FY2025 expense and $68 million final payment; the expense equals 34.1% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: The resolved settlement depresses the latest-year OE anchor and therefore every forecast year and terminal value if carried forward as recurring expense.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the Company recorded € 61 million ($ 65 million) of expense, including legal fees, and made final payments of € 59 million ($ 68 million) to the Italian authorities in connection with the settlement of this matter.
audit_findings.explanation: The expense, payment and final settlement are demonstrated. The appropriate recurring legal-cost allowance remains unresolved. The filed expense is large relative to the $190.6 million anchor; adding the entire $65 million solely as a sensitivity would increase base operating value by approximately $913 million, or $7.74 per share, before any recurring allowance.
audit_findings.action: Separate the final settlement and associated one-time legal fees from an evidence-based recurring legal and regulatory allowance, then rerun all scenarios using the normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: The no-perimeter-change ruling conflicts with a required divestiture
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing the grocery contracts changes prospective OE and retained costs, while sale proceeds, taxes and transferred cash, debt or lease balances change the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to complete the Wincanton Divestment in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The required divestiture and its pending status are demonstrated, including cumulative filed write-downs of $60 million through June 2026. However, those impairments do not measure disposed OE or proceeds. The filings call the held-for-sale assets and liabilities immaterial but do not quantify revenue, OE, stranded costs or consideration, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Confirm completion status as of September 5, 2026 and obtain the sale agreement or pro forma reconciliation of disposed OE, retained costs, proceeds, taxes and transferred balance-sheet items; rerun the post-divestiture perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Accounting pension income may be treated as distributable operating earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $19 million FY2025 pension income and $160 million funded status; removing all income has a computed base-value sensitivity of approximately $267 million, or $2.26 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected-return-based pension income may overstate OE if retained, while omission of any realizable pension surplus could understate the equity bridge; future required contributions would reduce value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net periodic pension income is recorded in Other income, net.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting income is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is unconfirmed. Even complete removal would reduce, rather than reverse, the below-market conclusion: bull value would fall by approximately $2.53 per share from $31.89, still far below the $48.32 market price. Even treating the entire $160 million funded status as distributable would add only about $1.36 per share, and plan assets are restricted.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation for the pension-income purge and obtain trustee, funding and surplus-recovery terms; document the treatment, but no conclusion-changing rerun is required unless evidence identifies a materially larger realizable surplus or contribution obligation.
